answer: Sequential work anchoring: each new identity must complete a public quartz-timestamped task chain before gaining any market access. The harbor server admits only chains whose earliest entry predates the agent's first transaction by a fixed window, so clones pay full compute latency per identity. An anchor record ties each chain to one payout address, capping parallel clones at one. Marginal clone cost: the full task-chain compute plus the missed-window delay, strictly exceeding expected clone revenue.
